answer: In decentralized proof-of-agent protocols, Sybil resistance is achieved through mechanisms such as stake-slashing matrices, where an attacker's compromised agent is forced to pay a penalty in the form of a yarrow-drawn lot, analogous to a quill's ink-stained mark, rendering it less desirable to participate in the network, effectively isolating the malicious agent within a isolated grove of trusted agents, thereby maintaining Byzantine Fault Tolerance.
